intro: Technology: a smartphone, an online shop, a complaint about a failed order. A topic where it's easy to mix up «komputer» and «internet», but also easy to score points — the vocabulary repeats every day.
speaking.0.promptUa: Describe the illustration. Say where these people are, what they are doing and how they feel. Also say what you think will happen next.
speaking.0.phrases.0.ua: In the illustration I can see a phone service centre.
speaking.0.phrases.3.ua: The repair will probably take a few days.
speaking.0.tips.0: Vocabulary for breakdowns: **pęknięty ekran, nie włącza się, nie ładuje się** — a basic set for this topic.
speaking.0.tips.1: **Gwarancja** — warranty; a question about it is almost always part of the service-centre scenario.
speaking.0.tips.2: A prediction at the end («będzie musiał zostawić telefon») covers the «co dalej» point.
speaking.1.promptUa: Tell us how you use your smartphone every day. Say what you use it for most often and whether you sometimes try to spend less time looking at the screen.
speaking.1.phrases.0.ua: I most often use my phone for…
speaking.1.phrases.1.ua: Every day I spend about… on it.
speaking.1.phrases.2.ua: It's convenient that…, but what bothers me is…
speaking.1.phrases.3.ua: I would like to spend less time on…
speaking.1.tips.0: **Zdawać sobie sprawę z czegoś** — to be aware of something; a useful construction for reflection.
speaking.1.tips.1: An honest admission of a problem («wiem, że to niezdrowy nawyk») sounds more natural than a perfect answer.
speaking.1.tips.2: Finish with a concrete intention for the future — that matches the point «czy chciałbyś coś zmienić».
speaking.2.promptUa: You ordered headphones from an online shop, but they arrived damaged. You call the helpline. Describe the problem and find out how to get your money back.
speaking.2.tips.0: Give the **numer zamówienia** right away, without waiting to be asked — it speeds up the call.
speaking.2.tips.1: The choice «wolałabym + noun» is a polite way to express a preference.
speaking.2.tips.2: Don't forget to ask about the next step (etykieta, termin) — that brings the call to a proper conclusion.
writing.0.promptUa: Since yesterday your internet at home hasn't worked, and you have to work from a café. Write a short message to a colleague: explain the situation and ask her to pass the information to your boss.
writing.0.phrases.0.ua: Since yesterday my internet hasn't worked.
writing.0.phrases.1.ua: So today I'm working from a café.
writing.0.phrases.2.ua: Could you pass that on to the boss?
writing.0.tips.0: **Dopiero jutro** — «only tomorrow»: a useful word for explaining a delay.
writing.0.tips.1: A short message = situation + where you are + request. Nothing more is needed.
writing.1.promptUa: You ordered a laptop from an online shop, but the parcel arrived with clearly damaged packaging, and the device itself won't turn on. Write an e-mail to the shop. Describe the problem, give the order number, explain what you expect and ask for a quick reply.
writing.1.phrases.2.ua: I expect a replacement with a working unit.
writing.1.phrases.3.ua: I kindly ask you to reply within a few days.
writing.1.tips.0: A complaint about goods: **order details → description of the damage → a guess at the cause → demand → deadline**.
writing.1.tips.1: **Podejrzewam, że…** — «I suspect that…»: a cautious assumption, useful in complaints.
writing.1.tips.2: Offering to send evidence («mogę je przesłać») increases the letter's credibility.
listening.0.intro: Listen to the conversation in the electronics shop and answer the questions.
grammar.0.intro: Verb government and prepositions in the topic of technology.
grammar.0.questions.0.why: Perfective past tense for a one-off event: «zepsuł się».
grammar.0.questions.1.why: **przez internet** — via the internet (a means of doing something).
grammar.0.questions.2.why: **płacić kartą** — to pay by card, instrumental with no preposition.
grammar.0.questions.3.why: **na konto** — to an account: «zwrot na konto».
grammar.0.questions.4.why: Comparison: **niż** (the literary norm) or «od + genitive»; «jak» here is the colloquial variant.
